item.title: Denmark first in EU to end mother-to-child HIV transmission
item.description: Denmark is the first country in the EU to eliminate mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis, according to Statens Serum Institut (SSI). For years, Denmark has conducted regular screening of pregnant women and ensured rapid treatment, meaning children are no longer born with these infections. item.title: Cancelled royal ball donates food to charity
item.description: A royal gala scheduled for Friday was canceled after Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called an election. The Royal House announced that most food has been frozen for later use or returned to suppliers, while perishables intended for staff were donated to Kirkens Korshær (DanChurchSocial). item.title: A short guide to eating mindfully in Copenhagen
item.description: Copenhagen is usually considered one of the world’s capitals of food, but things are more complicated. Juggling high prices, discounts, and numerous food events may not be easy. These are some tips from food culture writer Kiki Canuto.

item.title: Turning cultural friction into practical support for internationals
item.description: Raised in a Caribbean community where belonging felt automatic, Marie Sorivelle has spent the past fourteen years navigating Denmark’s systems and rethinking what community looks like when it must be built intentionally. That’s why she is founding Haven, to help internationals navigate systems in Denmark.

item.description: The distribution company Dao aims to deliver all election cards five days before the general election on March 24. item.title: Løkke: 8,000 Danes now on Middle East registry
item.description: Approximately 8,000 Danes are registered on the “Danes List” in the Middle East, a sharp increase from 3,000 two days ago. item.title: Aarhus officially removes Eskimovej from the city map
item.description: On Monday, Eskimovej in Aarhus officially changes its name to Silavej. The municipality is implementing the change following a request from the Greenlandic House and the student association Avalak, who argue the term “eskimo” is outdated and offensive. “Sila” was chosen as a neutral alternative, meaning weather, world, or mindset in Greenlandic. item.description: Oil prices surged in Asian trading on Monday following large-scale US and Israeli attacks on Iran. Brent crude rose 13% to $82 per barrel, its highest price since January 2025. item.title: More foreign master’s grads find work in Denmark
item.description: A new analysis from the Confederation of Danish Industry shows a record number of international Master’s students staying to work in Denmark. According to 2024 data, 53% were employed two years after graduation, up from 37-40% between 2014 and 2019. Meanwhile, 37% left the country and 10% remain without employment.
